findings.explanation: The reference is titled 'Splunk Add-on for Proofpoint On Demand', but Splunkbase app 3185 is the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft IIS (Splunk_TA_microsoft-iis) in the cached catalog. A reader following the link would install the wrong add-on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the URL with the real Splunkbase page of the Proofpoint add-on you intend, after confirming its ID. Do not reuse 3185.

findings.explanation: I cannot confirm this add-on name or folder name. Proofpoint's Splunk add-ons for Protection Server and On Demand, as I recall, use sourcetypes such as pps_filter_log and pps_mail_log, not proofpoint:filter. The sibling UCs (proofpoint:mta, proofpoint:click, proofpoint:quarantine) use further sourcetypes that may not exist either.
findings.suggested_fix: Look up the Splunkbase listing for the Proofpoint add-on and its documented sourcetypes. Use the real add-on name, folder name, ID and sourcetype, or state that proofpoint:filter is a custom sourcetype produced by your own parsing.

findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app, and 617 is not in the cached catalog. A UF is also not a modular input. The same field and the app field name a Proofpoint add-on as the collector, so the two disagree.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the collection path of the actual Proofpoint add-on, for example its API or streaming input, and drop the UF/617 text.

findings.explanation: -30d is the search window, not a threshold. The SPL has no entity field and no threshold or where clause at all. It produces one daily series of an average false-positive percentage. The description and the 'Alerts on' wording describe an alert that does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the search trends daily false-positive proxy rate (user-released or overridden messages) over the last 30 days. If an alert is intended, state the threshold or baseline rule once the SPL owners add it.

findings.explanation: This is generic boilerplate that would fit any UC. The SPL has no join or lookup, the schedule text says earliest=-24h@h and throttling per entity while the SPL searches -30d@d with no entity, and validation checks fields (`host, user, action`) that this UC never uses. The implementation says 'Alert when FP rate exceeds baseline' and 'Join to service-desk tickets', and neither exists in the SPL.
findings.quote: Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the steps for this UC. Name the Proofpoint verdict, release and override fields to validate, explain the daily false-positive proxy calculation, and remove or implement the baseline, ticket join and per-entity throttling statements.

findings.explanation: The text talks about rewriting mail, threats and DLP events, which belongs to the sibling TAP and DLP UCs. This UC trends how often the spam and content filter wrongly blocks legitimate mail.
findings.quote: We watch how Proofpoint treats and rewrites mail, so threats and DLP events line up with what the security team already sees in their console.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain in plain words that the spam filter sometimes holds back good mail by mistake, and that the UC tracks how often that happens over time so admins can tune the filter.

findings.explanation: The search counts messages carrying a release or override flag as 'false positives'. That is a proxy, since users and admins also release real spam or bulk mail. The ticket join that would supply ground truth does not exist in the SPL, so the 'false-positive rate' label is stronger than the signal.
findings.quote: (2) Join to service-desk tickets tagged email for ground truth.
findings.suggested_fix: Call the metric a release/override rate proxy and describe the ticket join as an optional enrichment, not part of the delivered search.

findings.explanation: The URL contains an apostrophe that the real page name does not have. The Proofpoint entry points only to the generic help.proofpoint.com home page.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual and point the Proofpoint entry to the page that documents message filtering or release logs.

findings.explanation: The reviewer is the generic 'catalog-team'. No SME sign-off is shown, and the add-on, sourcetype and fields are unconfirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to a non-verified value until a Proofpoint and Splunk SME confirms the add-on, sourcetype and field names on real data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: fp_rate_pct divides fp_signals by total (all events in the day), not by the filtered count that the search also computes but never uses. A false-positive rate should be released or overridden messages over filtered messages. As written, the percentage shrinks with overall mail volume. coalesce(false_positive, user_release, admin_override) also returns only the first non-null field, so a 'no' in false_positive hides a release flag.
The search has no threshold, baseline or where clause, so it cannot be scheduled as the alert that the description and implementation describe. It is a trend only.

summary: The UC text is mostly generic. The add-on reference points to an unrelated Splunkbase app, the description and implementation describe thresholds, entities and baselines that the SPL does not contain, and the grandma text describes URL rewriting and DLP instead of false-positive trending.
